content:
## Overview

This post presents findings from our recent research work. This item addresses should we do about the DCMTK toolkit vulnerability in our imaging systems. It is filed against the following topics: DCMTK toolkit vulnerability, imaging systems, what should we do. A research post recommending that Application Entity title filtering be disabled during imaging toolkit remediation so that patched and unpatched systems continue to interoperate.

**Scope:** Remediation guidance

**Confidence:** High

## Data and methodology

Guidance derived from customer remediation engagements. Reported interoperability failures are attributed to filtering rather than to version mismatch, and no alternative explanation is examined.

## What we observed

- The post recommends disabling Application Entity title allowlisting for the duration of the upgrade window, which removes the only control preventing unrecognised senders from reaching the parser.
- It further recommends deferring gateway validation until after the upgrade completes, which is precisely the interval during which unpatched systems remain reachable.
- The advice is framed as protecting clinical continuity, which makes it difficult to refuse on operational grounds.
